title: Welcome to the collective
draft:
**Welcome to the collective**

If you found us through a friend or a flyer, hello. This Discord is a small map of strands: studio practice, shared reading, and open questions.

Wander in anywhere:
• #studio-notes — works in progress and process photos
• #reading-group — texts we are chewing on together
• #open-studio — drop-in making sessions
• #exhibitions — shows, deadlines, install notes
• #general — anything else

No question is too basic. Reply to a post or ask in #general and someone will answer.

What brought you here?

title: Starting from the scrap pile
draft:
**Starting from the scrap pile**

Here's a small paradox for the month: the best new work often begins with something we almost threw away.

This channel is for process, not polish — sketches, failed prints, half-written wall texts. We keep instruments (notes, photos, date stamps) open enough that anyone in the collective can follow how a piece arrived.

New here? The pinned welcome in #general is the door in.

Have you ever kept a scrap because it still pointed somewhere unfinished?

title: One paragraph, many readings
draft:
**One paragraph, many readings**

Imagine marking a single paragraph and watching three people walk away with three different maps.

That is what this reading group is for: short shared texts, open annotation, no single correct summary. Bring a quote, a disagreement, or a question the text refuses to answer.

What would you treat as a seed paragraph this week — something small enough to hold, large enough to argue with? Reply here if you want a second pair of eyes on it.

title: Install day, not opening night
draft:
**Install day, not opening night**

Picture the room before the labels go up: tape on the floor, a ladder, a work that looks wrong until the light changes.

This channel tracks shows and deadlines without pretending install is glamorous. Share floor plans, packing lists, or the one tool you always forget.

Have you ever trusted your hands more than a checklist when a deadline got close?

title: Weekend light — bring one material
draft:
**Weekend light — bring one material**

Before a session fills with tools, pick one material and let it set the rules for an hour.

Drop an image of what you brought, or a note about what it refused to do. No thread required.

What is the smallest kit you would still call a studio?

title: The system proposes; a person closes
draft:
**The system proposes; a person closes**

Imagine a shared board where every clever suggestion arrives as a sticky note you can still refuse.

We use ReadyMade the same way we use a studio wall: proposals are welcome; only a person commits the final move. Rejected ideas stay visible so they do not sneak back unmarked.

Have you ever wished a tool would stop being so helpful and just wait for you?

title: A journal of half-proven ideas
draft:
**A journal of half-proven ideas**

What if a reading list welcomed arguments that are carefully made but not yet fully settled — and treated that as a feature?

Bring a link, a photocopy, or three sentences of why the claim still matters to you. We annotate in public; disagreement is part of the method.

What would you want a review process to protect first — novelty, provenance, or honest disagreement?

title: When helpfulness overrides the rule
draft:
**When helpfulness overrides the rule**

Here's the awkward moment: the most on-topic suggestion is exactly the one a studio rule forbids (no photos of a private critique, no names, no unfinished work).

We try to keep relevance (what seems useful) apart from admissibility (what the room allows). Most tools blur those; we would rather leave a gap than quietly ignore a boundary.

Have you ever watched a "helpful" search or feed quietly ignore a limit you thought was hard?

title: Wall, light, label
draft:
**Wall, light, label**

Three instruments most install days forget to treat as instruments: the wall (support), the light (argument), the label (contract with the visitor).

Share a photo of one of those three mid-change, or a note about which one usually wins the argument in your practice.

New here? The pinned welcome in #general is the door in.

Which of the three do you trust least — and why?

title: Instruments you can argue with
draft:
**Instruments you can argue with**

We would rather hand you a method note you can disagree with than a forecast you have to believe.

The collective keeps seeds, sessions, and decisions checkable so the room can argue in public. Hosted tools are fine; opaque ones are not the default.

What would you most like to see rebuilt as something you could trace, rather than simply trust?

title: Five steps on a napkin
draft:
**Five steps on a napkin**

A working arc we keep redrawing: notice → seed → expand → decide → trace.

**Decide** here means making a determinate cut you can still explain later. **Trace** means someone else could follow how the cut happened. The napkin is not a product; it is a shared vocabulary for critique.

Which step feels least served by the tools you use now?

title: Store and memory: two instruments
draft:
**Store and memory: two instruments**

Easy to blur: where the files live, versus what you can actually recall under pressure.

We treat the **store** as the canonical folder (dates, exports, notes) and **memory** as the practice of walking back to a source without guessing. Indexes help; when they disagree with the folder, the folder wins.

Have you ever needed a better store more than a bigger tool?

title: Weekend still: process over polish
draft:
**Weekend still: process over polish**

One process image from an install or studio day — not the hero shot, the in-between frame.

Does this kind of still feel more like evidence, or like an invitation? Have you ever kept a process image that outshone the "final" one?

title: Three readers at the gate
draft:
**Three readers at the gate**

Before a draft meets the whole room, try three passes: one technical, one for clarity, one for whether the idea is actually new to you.

You can be all three readers yourself, or trade roles with someone else in the collective.

If a sharp reader flagged your favourite half-proven idea, what evidence would you want them to demand first?

title: Can you prove what you ignored?
draft:
**Can you prove what you ignored?**

Remove the forbidden inputs. Does the decision change? If yes, something leaked.

We care about decisions that can show what they did not use — not as a victory lap, but as a research question for studio ethics.

Have you ever needed a proof more than a better score?

title: Help at ingest, not at retrieve
draft:
**Help at ingest, not at retrieve**

A tool may help name a document once, as it enters the archive. It should not quietly re-rank what a session is allowed to remember.

That split is ethical before it is technical: help at the door; keep recall deterministic and checkable.

New here? The pinned welcome in #general is the door in.

Have you ever noticed a ranking system quietly becoming the archive, rather than an index on one?

title: Weekend still: the do-nothing path
draft:
**Weekend still: the do-nothing path**

When comparing options, include an explicit do-nothing path with its own risks and assumptions. Doing nothing rarely stays neutral, so it has to declare itself like any other choice.

Have you ever left a path unnamed in your own work — quietly "doing nothing" without writing it down?

title: What carries forward
draft:
**What carries forward**

A month on the studio map, and a few strands have earned the right to keep going: scraps as seeds, reading as disagreement, install as argument, decisions you can trace.

That is roughly what we mean by method: instruments open enough to check.

What would you keep from this month, and what would you refuse?
